sn10.2:1.2: The suffix _-nāmaka_ is a slight. Compare “Senior in name only” ([sn21.10:1.2]()) and _nāmaka_ in the sense “mere words” ([mn80:15.5](), [mn99:10.5]()). His verse is similar to that of Māra in [sn4.14]().
sn10.2:3.2: The Buddha avoids _nāmaka_ and politely calls him “Sakka”.
sn10.2:3.4: Accepting the variant _ananukampituṁ_ at [ne37:194.4](), which is endorsed by that text’s commentaries. The text as stands enjoins lack of compassion, which cannot be right.
